caption: The drawing depicts an aerial view of a landscaped area featuring a mix of geometric and organic elements. The composition is dominated by a large green field occupying the lower two-thirds of the image, sparsely dotted with individual green trees and a few clusters of darker, denser foliage. At the top edge of the field, there are several intersecting straight beige or light brown paths forming a grid, inside of which rectangular and triangular beds contain symmetrically arranged vegetation, including multicolored flowerbeds marked with pink, yellow, and red hues. Along the paths and boundaries, rows of evenly spaced green trees or shrubs are illustrated with circular canopies. Near the upper right side, there are two brownish structures, likely buildings, surrounded by more trees and some shaded land contours suggesting elevation change or terrain. The background areas bordering the field and landscaped section are filled with a solid tan color, indicating a different ground surface or boundary. The drawing uses mainly green, tan, brown, and accent colors to represent vegetation, pathways, structures, and open land.
title: Eliza B. Jumel Estate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
